can_answer_question: partly: this data has no miles-driven exposure, so it cannot measure deaths per mile or whether per-mile risk declined; it can show the annual number of reported crashes with at least one motorist death as a crash-count trend.
metric: Annual number of police-reported NYC crashes with at least one motorist reported killed (number_of_motorist_killed > 0).
denominator: None; this is a crash count, not a rate.
population: Police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes dated 2013 through 2025, inclusive; the metric counts the subset with at least one motorist reported killed.
years: 2013-2025 inclusive; check whether either endpoint year is only partially covered.

data_check.facts: The planned period contains 2,132,218 source crash rows. Each year 2013-2025 has observed dates from January 1 through December 31; no edge year is visibly partial by its observed date bounds. Within the planned population, crash_date is non-missing by the year filter, no checked sentinel date occurs, and number_of_motorist_killed is missing in 0 rows in every year.
data_check.decision: No change to the plan. Keep all crashes as the year-specific source population and count the subset whose motorist-deaths value is positive. No rows need to be removed for a missing classification field.
data_check.plan_change: Clarified the row population as all crashes in the planned years and the fatal-crash condition as the metric criterion, so population row counts can be checked without counting rows by the death value; the substantive metric is unchanged.

limitations: The crash file has no vehicle-miles-traveled or other mileage exposure, so a count of fatal crashes is not a per-mile risk or rate. This metric counts fatal crash events, not the number of motorists killed. Full-year observed date bounds do not establish record completeness or absence of within-year gaps.
